title: The Penitent Knight
text: A knight of the Court walks barefoot in chains, his feet bloody from the stones, his surcoat sewn with the names of the dead. He does penance, he says, for what he did. He asks to fight beside you and earn his forgiveness in blood.

options.label: Let him earn his forgiveness at your side, and spend his blood before yours.

outcomes.text: He fights like a man with nothing left to lose, and puts himself in front of every blow.

options.label: The wisest asks him what he did, before anyone trusts him with their back.

outcomes.text: Something terrible. He tells it all, then tells you where the Court keeps its secrets, as if one confession demanded another.

options.label: Refuse him. Whatever he did, it is not yours to forgive.

outcomes.text: He walks on, chains dragging, and kneels to pray for the Leader anyway. It helps, which is somehow worse.

options.label: Our own Knight hears his oath, knight to knight, and binds it to their own.

outcomes.text: Two knights kneel in the road, and the penitent's oath binds to the Knight's. He walks away forgiven. The Knight walks away harder to break.
